blocks.text: To get more information about a chart in a dashboard or report, click an item on the chart and click Analyze Chart. The chart is displayed in an Insights page where you can interactively drill down to specific transactions. Alternatively, you can start an analysis by going to the Logs tab of any Insights page.
To learn more about the Insights pages, see About Insights.

Let's take the following Web Insights instance to walk you through the Insights pages. This is what the default Web Insights page looks like. It shows a trend chart for the data type Overall Traffic. The chart shows the overall traffic for the current day in terms of transactions.
On any Insights page, you can do the following:

blocks.item: At any time, you can choose different options to display the metrics you want to see. For example, let's say you want to change the timeframe and the chart type in the Web Insights instance. The following image shows the timeframe customized to the previous month, and the chart type has been changed to a pie chart. Even though these options have been changed, you're still viewing Overall Traffic, but it's now for the custom dates selected.

You can also choose a different data type from the drop-down menu. The following image shows a new data type, Advanced Threat Category, is selected. After that data type is selected, the pie chart changes to reflect the results of your selection. You're now seeing the Advanced Threat Category traffic for the custom dates selected. As you edit the chart, your workflow is recorded in the history bar below the chart.

There are a number of ways to interactively drill down and get more granular data. Each data type has its own set of filters, located on the left pane. If you look at the filters for Advanced Threat Category, you see one of them is User. The following image shows the filter User is selected. Think of data types as the "Grouped by..." section, so the image shows Any users, grouped by Advanced Threat Category for the custom dates selected.

The image shows the category Malicious Content portion. You can click on that portion, or any other portion, for a closer drilldown. When you select the Malicious Content portion, the portion's drop-down menu reveals the data types you can choose from for that portion. The User data type is selected.

After selecting User, the pie chart changes. You're now seeing traffic for the Advanced Threat Category, specifically for Malicious Content, grouped by Users. There are 5 users displayed that have contributed to the Malicious Content category for the custom dates selected, while the rest are categorized as Other.

If you want a closer look at one of the users, you can drill down further by clicking on a user, and selecting from the options displayed in the portion's drop-down menu. The following image shows a selected user. You can click View Logs from the portion's drop-down menu to look at that user's Malicious Content category logs.
After you click View Logs, you are directed to the Logs page. The following image displays the user's Malicious Content category logs. To learn more about the Logs pages, see About Insights Logs.
You can also start a new analysis or change the focus of your investigation, as follows:

Click Start Over to go back to the default chart. The data type menu above the chart is set to Overall Traffic, filters are reset, and all charts, except the default, are deleted from the history bar.
Choose a different data type from the menu at the top. This automatically resets the filters.

As you work with your data, the tool records the workflow in the history bar below the chart. Every time you make a change to the chart, such as adding a filter or changing the chart type, a previous version is added to the history bar. You can then click any previous chart in the history bar to see it again. If you view an earlier version and change it, all subsequent versions are automatically deleted. This enables an administrator to review the various stages of the investigation and change direction for the analysis upon review, if necessary. The history bar can retain up to 50 versions of the chart. If there are more than 50 versions, the oldest versions are deleted as new ones are added. The chart icons are numbered, so you can track how many versions you have.
Click Print View to print the entire sequence of charts in the history bar.
